About the ACDB

The ACDB (Animal Culture Database) is a database of variables on socially learned behavioral traditions in wild animal populations worldwide. It brings together the current literature on behavioral variation within species, in contexts such as communication, foraging, and migration. The data are open access and can be explored on this website.

Document

Record socially transmitted behaviors observed in wild animal populations.

Analyze

Examine patterns of cultural diversity across the globe and across species.

Inform

Use what we know about animal culture to support biodiversity conservation.

How the data are organized

The database has four tables: groups, species, behaviors, and sources. A group is a population of one species that shares one or more traditions. Each behavior belongs to a group and cites the sources that support it. The codebook defines every variable. The tables can be downloaded as CSV: species, groups, behaviors, and sources.

Versions and updates

Major releases (e.g. v1.0.0, v2.0.0) are based on the addition of 100 or more populations. Minor releases (e.g. v1.1.0) are based on the addition of fewer than 100 populations. Changes to the contents of the database, such as a missing paper, a taxonomy fix, or a new location, are patches (e.g. v1.1.1). We plan to cover most of the existing animal behavior literature in version 2.0, and we are building a pipeline for external contributions.

Who we are

The ACDB was developed at the University of Arizona. Contact Dr. Basava about the data and Dr. Román-Palacios about the website.
